summary: No restricted construction survives (the whitelisted 'probeerde na te denken' is accepted) and the only hard word is the inflated 'metalen'. Remaining issues are naturalness: 'een hele magische wereld' invites the 'very magical' reading, a book that 'zei', the collocation 'uitleg voor', and a verbless fragment after the dash.

findings.problem: 'metalen' is listed hard (B2); a plain rephrase with the known noun exists.
findings.evidence: lexicon: metalen hard B2, metaal known A2 — regular material adjective, so should_fix rather than must_fix
findings.required_fix: Write 'Een platte plaat van metaal op een deur nodigt uit tot duwen.'

findings.problem: Inflected 'hele' before an adjective is read by many readers as colloquial 'very' (a very magical world), not 'whole'.
findings.evidence: V1 and V3 notes avoid this form for the same reason
findings.required_fix: Write 'een hele wereld vol magie' (or 'een complete magische wereld').

findings.problem: English 'one of his books had said' copied; in Dutch a book does not 'zeggen', the idiom is 'stond in'.
findings.evidence: EN: 'one of his books had said' vs NL: 'zei een van zijn boeken'
findings.required_fix: Write '\emph{Geloof niet al je gedachten,} stond in een van zijn boeken.'

findings.fragment: Dan was er een uitleg voor de brief zonder postzegel in de brievenbus.
findings.problem: 'uitleg voor' is not the collocation for an explanation of a fact; Dutch says 'een verklaring voor', and the long noun phrase after it is heavy.
findings.evidence: lexicon: verklaring known; 'uitleg' = explanation given by someone
findings.required_fix: Write 'Dan was er een verklaring voor de brief zonder postzegel.' or 'Dan was het duidelijk: zo kwam de brief zonder postzegel in de brievenbus.'

findings.fragment: —geen excuus vooraf: ‘misschien komt er geen professor’, of ‘misschien kan de professor alleen maar lepels buigen’.
findings.problem: Verbless fragment hung on the em dash; an A2 reader has to supply the verb and the subject.
findings.evidence: the dash joins a full clause to a bare noun phrase with a colon list
findings.required_fix: Give it a verb: '—ze bedacht vooraf geen excuus: ‘misschien komt er geen professor’, of ‘misschien kan de professor alleen maar lepels buigen’.'

findings.problem: Gloss on a lemma the lexicon marks known A2.
findings.required_fix: Drop the \gl wrapper and the @glosses line.

findings.problem: Tool status unknown, but 'universum' is a transparent cognate already used in the glossary.
findings.evidence: lexicon: universum absent; glossary.json Confundus Charm note uses 'het hele universum'
findings.required_fix: Keep; lexicon owner: add 'universum' as known.

findings.fragment: een testbare hypothese … die ga je testen
findings.problem: Tool rows 'testbaar' (unknown) and 'testen' (gloss-or-replace) are dismissed: testbaar = known 'test' + -baar, and 'de hypothese testen' is the fixed glossary phrase.
findings.evidence: lexicon: test A2 known; glossary.json hypothese: 'test the hypothesis' = 'de hypothese testen'

findings.problem: Bare 'merkte:' is abrupt; the perception verb wants its object.
findings.evidence: V1/V3 'Harry merkte het bij zichzelf:' reads smoother
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'Harry merkte het bij zichzelf: hij \emph{verwachtte} het gewoon.'

findings.problem: A handle is attached 'aan' a door; 'op' fits the flat plate only.
findings.evidence: V3 uses 'een handvat aan een deur'
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'Een handvat aan een deur nodigt uit tot trekken.'

findings.problem: 'excuus' primarily means apology; the precise everyday word for a pretext, 'smoes', is known A2.
R-TE-INF review flag accepted: 'proberen te' is the whitelisted review chunk and the alternatives ('wilde nadenken', 'dacht na') change attempt into intention or success.
findings.required_fix: Keep. For exceptions.json: consider promoting 'proberen te' to treat_as vocabulary; it was accepted in two of three versions.
